en.html:
In the sky, on the ground—war.

Blood washing away blood. Mountains of corpses. For once, the expression was not making any exaggeration.

Below, archers shot gaps into the enemy lines. Through them came men in masses, long weapons together, mounted commanders leading. Above, warriors picked worthy opponents, announced their names, split clouds and rode the wind into fierce sword exchanges.

War.
From the age called medieval.

Look more closely, and the period could be narrowed down. Tsurugi shapes, styles of combat, the infantry's weapons and dress. Neither the Genpei War nor the struggles of the Sengoku lords fitted these things.

Above all, the banners.
Rich brocade. Gold sun, red field.

Both sides had them.

Even in Yamato's history, not many times had this arrangement occurred. Not many wars.

ja.html:
天と地で、争いが繰り広げられていた。
　血で血を洗う――屍山を築くという表現がまさしく
相応しい。

　地上では、射手が矢を射かけ、敵陣に間隙を穿つや、
騎馬の将帥率いる兵の群れが長物を連ねて押し進む。
　天空では、互いを好敵と見定めた武者同士が名乗り
合い、雲を裂き風に乗って、激しく太刀を打ち交わす。

　戦争の光景だ。
　中世……そう呼ばれる時代の。

　詳細に観察すれば、より正確な区分も可能だった。
　劒冑の形状、武者の戦闘形式、歩兵の武器装束――
それらはこの戦争が源平合戦でも戦国大名の抗争でも
ないことを如実に語っている。

　何よりも、戦場に散見する旗……
　赤地に金で日輪を描いた豪奢な錦織。

　それが、<ruby>どちらの陣営にも存在する<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。
　そんな事態、そんな戦争が起きた時代は、大和史上
にも稀であった。

Muramasa I"In the end, the righteous win. The world is made that way."
Muramasa II"..."

Muramasa I"You must."

Muramasa I"...I see."
Muramasa II"Let us go home, Father. The battle is over."
Muramasa I"Yes..."
Muramasa"Over?"

en.html:
A simple house in a backcountry Emishi village.

The visitor had the bearing of a formidable warrior. Surely a commander with a district and an army in his charge. Between such a man and an ordinary Emishi, the difference in station ought to be earth and sky.

The householder did not even stand.
A proper greeting? That also, no.

And the warrior took no offense.
...Achha. Was that the sort of relationship?

Earth and sky, certainly. But the sky had come to visit, and the earth could not be bothered to get up. All my understanding of rank was standing there very properly, waiting for somebody to be offended. Neither man obliged. Between friends, apparently, even the social order could be told: shoes off, sit quietly.

Muramasa I"You are safe. That is what matters."
Akima"You were watching?"
Muramasa I"Yes."
Akima"Sasaki, what a fellow. Time and place for betrayal, never once does he get those wrong."
Akima"At least a rank or two the Yoshino people could have given generously. His complaints they kept waving away. Now see."
Muramasa I"Such profit-eating fellows, who needs them? If he is going to change sides anyway, put him on the enemy side from the beginning. Less confusion."
Akima"...His own logic he follows, though. Land he wants, rank he wants. North to south, south to north, full running about. All to protect his clan."
Muramasa I"Whole thing ulta! A commander uses his clan's strength to protect the greater cause."
Muramasa I"Throw away the cause to protect the clan, and still call yourself a warrior? On what basis?"
Akima"Yes..."
Muramasa I"You would not change to the Northern Court, Akima saab, even if every last member of your clan and following were to die."
Akima"Naturally not."
Muramasa I"This province of Ise lies at the Grand Shrine's feet. Nowhere do the people revere the Emperor more strongly, or hate rebels more deeply."
Muramasa I"To a false emperor, our heads will not bend. Bilkul nahin."
Akima"Yes."
Muramasa I"We must win..."
Akima"For that, Muramasa, your strength is needed."
Muramasa I"..."
Akima"His Majesty says nothing, but he seems to be waiting impatiently. Kusunoki also."
Muramasa I"Yes..."

Akima"The head smith of Sengo village, Kuwana, in Ise—Gorou Masamune come again, they said. His Majesty heard it. The imperial command came: forge a tsurugi. Three years now."
Akima"Still not ready?"
Muramasa I"Not yet."
Akima"Put Kusunoki in your tsurugi and send him out at the head of the whole Southern army: the Northern Court would vanish in a single night."
Akima"The peace Yamato's people have been waiting for would come at last..."
Muramasa I"I also believe it must be so. That is exactly why I cannot just pick up the hammer and begin."
Muramasa I"No second try is waiting for me..."
Akima"Still unable to devise it?"
Muramasa I"More a matter of direction."
Akima"Direction?"
Muramasa I"Akima saab, what do you consider the supreme tsurugi?"
Akima"Great strength, hard armor, wings swift and sharp—"
Muramasa I"And this thing can actually be made, you think?"
Akima"...No."
Muramasa I"However clever the smith, he cannot hammer out 'everything, please.' One thing you choose, another you give up. It has to be done."
Akima"And you cannot settle the choice?"
Muramasa I"Yes."
Akima"What is best, what is supreme... is that the question?"
Muramasa I"The supreme tsurugi, Akima saab? The one that does its work. That is all."
Muramasa I"Who must it help? Who must it destroy? ...First make that clear. Otherwise nothing begins."
Akima"The Southern Court is our ally, the Northern Court our enemy, surely?"
Muramasa I"More deeply. More exactly. Purpose clear, abilities can be made more specialized. The clearer the work, the better I can shape the tsurugi for it."

ja.html:
飽間「勢州桑名、千子村の鍛冶長かじおさは、五郎正宗の 再来ならん……。 　その風評が帝のお耳に届き、劒冑鍛造の勅 が下って――早三年」
飽間「まだ出来ぬか」
始祖村正「まだだ」
飽間「ぬしの劒冑を楠木殿が身に纏い、南朝全軍 を率いて押し出せば、北朝など一夜のうちに 滅び去ろう」
飽間「大和の民の待ち望む平穏がようやく訪れる であろう……」
始祖村正「うても、そうあらねばならぬと思うておる。 　だからこそ、軽々しく鍛造に踏み切れぬ」
始祖村正「やり直しは利かんからの……」
飽間「まだ工夫がつかぬか」
始祖村正「というよりも、方向よな」
飽間「方向？」
始祖村正「飽間様は、至高の劒冑とは如何なるものだ と思われる？」
飽間「力が強く、甲鉄は硬く、翼は鋭く速く――」
始祖村正「出来るとお思いか？」
飽間「……いや」
始祖村正「どれほど力量ある鍛冶師でも、万能の劒冑 は打てぬ。 　何かを選び、何かを捨てねばならぬ」
飽間「その選択が、定まらぬのか」
始祖村正「うむ」
飽間「何が最善、何が至高か……か？」
始祖村正「至高の劒冑とはな、飽間様。 　役目を遂げる劒冑・・・・・・・・に他ならぬ」
始祖村正「如何なる者の助けとなり、 　如何なる者を討ち滅ぼすのか、 　……まずそれを見定めねば、何も始まらぬ」
飽間「味方は南朝、敵は北朝であろう？」
始祖村正「より深く。より細かくだ。 　役目が明確であればあるほど、劒冑の性能 を特化できる」

en.html:
Akima"...I see."
Muramasa I"First know the purpose. Then decide the working. Bas, that is the matter."
Akima"Hence the visits to battlefields."
Muramasa I"Yes."
Akima"Will you arrive at a conclusion?"
Muramasa I"It will take more time. I still cannot see the enemy that must be defeated."
Muramasa I"Some turncoat like Sasaki is not enough."
Akima"I see... Very well. I shall let Kusunoki know your thinking, discreetly."
Akima"It will reach His Majesty also. Both should understand."
Muramasa I"I am sorry."
Akima"Arre, between you and me, what need for such distant words?"
Akima"You keep thinking, to your heart's content. Till then, these rebel armies I shall keep out of Yoshino."
Muramasa I"...I leave it to you."

飽間「帝のお耳にも入ろう。 　お二方とも納得される筈だ」

始祖村正「……頼む」

Muramasa II"...What!? Last month only Kusunoki captured it! After eight years His Majesty finally returned to Kyoto!"
Muramasa II"And Akamatsu's army was doing what? Guarding the capital was their appointed work!"
Muramasa I's Wife"That same Akamatsu changed sides."
Muramasa II"...What?"
Muramasa I"Sold them to the Northern Court, the bastard! The capital AND the Emperor!"
Muramasa II"The Emperor is in Northern hands!?"
